summary: This class examines Parashat Lekh Lekha (Bereshit chapter 15) through the commentary of Rashi on Berit Ben HaBetarim. It analyzes Rashi's calculation of the 400-year exile count starting from the birth of Yis'hak, the promise of ultimate judgment upon oppressing nations, and Avraham's peaceful passing. The lesson concludes with Rashi's explanation of divine patience regarding the sins of the Emori and a grammatical analysis of biblical verb tenses.
subjects: Calculation of the 400 years of exile
Ages of Kehat, Amram, and Moshe
questions: How does Rashi calculate the 400 years of exile foretold at Berit Ben HaBetarim?
Why were Bne Yisrael in Egypt for only 210 years if the prophecy promised 400 years?
What does the Torah mean when it says Avraham will join his ancestors in peace?
Why did God wait four generations before giving the Land of Israel to Avraham's descendants?
How does the position of an accent mark change a verb's tense in biblical Hebrew?
